key_works: Stokey, Lucas, and Prescott, 1989: Recursive Methods in Economic Dynamics, Harvard University Press
nominations.rationale: Stokey provided the indispensable mathematical foundation for dynamic programming and recursive competitive equilibrium in economics. Her rigorous synthesis enables every quantitative macroeconomist to compute and evaluate structural dynamic models.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of general equilibrium with incomplete markets and its welfare implications
key_works: Geanakoplos and Polemarchakis, 1986: Existence, regularity, and constrained suboptimality of competitive allocations when the asset market is incomplete, Essays in Honor of K.J. Arrow
nominations.rationale: They proved that when asset markets are incomplete, pecuniary externalities make competitive equilibria generically inefficient. This theoretical cornerstone provides the deep justification for macroeconomic interventions in heterogeneous-agent settings.

nominations.contribution: for the development and application of computable general equilibrium models
key_works: Shoven and Whalley, 1984: Applied General-Equilibrium Models of Taxation and International Trade, Journal of Economic Literature
nominations.rationale: They translated abstract Arrow-Debreu structures into operational tools calibrated to aggregate data, launching the field of applied general equilibrium. Their approach heavily informs how climate policy and trade impacts are quantified today.

key_works: Jackson and Wolinsky, 1996: A Strategic Model of Social and Economic Networks, Journal of Economic Theory
nominations.rationale: Jackson rigorously modeled how agent-level connections aggregate into systemic structures in equilibrium. His frameworks permit disciplined welfare evaluation of network architectures, providing a micro-foundation for contagion and inequality.

nominations.contribution: for his rigorous contributions to the measurement of economic inequality and mobility
key_works: Shorrocks, 1980: The Class of Additively Decomposable Inequality Measures, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: Shorrocks developed the axiomatic foundations for decomposing inequality and tracking wealth distributions over time. His precise measurement tools are essential to evaluate distributional counterfactuals generated by quantitative macro models.

nominations.rationale: Bewley's foundational models of general equilibrium with incomplete markets formalized the aggregate consequences of uninsurable idiosyncratic risk. nominations.rationale: His axiomatic approach to mechanism design and resource allocation provides mathematically precise solutions to the problems of fair division and public goods. It is a brilliant example of translating abstract welfare criteria into workable institutional rules.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to welfare economics, particularly regarding the natural environment and population
nominations.rationale: Dasgupta has rigorously integrated environmental constraints and natural capital into welfare economics and social choice. His models provide the formal, mechanism-based criteria necessary to evaluate the long-term real consequences of resource allocation.

key_works: Rubinstein, 1982: Perfect Equilibrium in a Bargaining Model, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: His integration of bounded rationality and bargaining frictions into equilibrium models deeply influenced how we analyze contract negotiations and information asymmetry. The precise theoretical mechanisms he developed are vital for understanding real-world institutional constraints.

nominations.contribution: for the measurement and analysis of intergenerational economic mobility

people.name: Gary Solon
people.affiliation: University of Michigan / University of Arizona

key_works: Solon, 1992: Intergenerational Income Mobility in the United States, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: His pioneering methodological work corrected life-cycle and measurement biases in intergenerational mobility estimation. This laid the empirical foundation for understanding how institutions and human capital shape long-run equality of opportunity.

nominations.contribution: for the empirical analysis and measurement of long-run income and wealth inequality
key_works: Piketty, 2003: Income Inequality in France, 1901-1998, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: His innovative assembly and analysis of centuries of historical tax register data completely reshaped the economics of distribution. This focus on long-run empirical trends is essential for mapping normative welfare criteria to policy debates on inequality.

nominations.contribution: for contributions to fair division and the normative theory of resource allocation
key_works: Moulin, 2003: Fair Division and Collective Welfare, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: He seamlessly integrated axiomatic normative theory with mechanism design to solve concrete problems of fair allocation. This structural approach to normative criteria ensures that theoretical welfare conclusions map practically to institutional design.

nominations.contribution: for the development of responsibility-sensitive egalitarianism and welfare economics
key_works: Fleurbaey, 2008: Fairness, Responsibility, and Welfare, Oxford University Press
nominations.rationale: His theoretical contributions allow welfare economics to formally separate factors within individual control from unobserved circumstances. This provides the exact normative foundation required to design optimal social insurance and education policies.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of general equilibrium with incomplete markets
key_works: Geanakoplos, 1990: An Introduction to General Equilibrium with Incomplete Markets, Journal of Mathematical Economics
nominations.rationale: He laid the theoretical foundation for modeling competitive equilibrium when risk markets are missing. Understanding these fundamental market failures is critical for any rigorous welfare evaluation of state-provided social insurance.

nominations.contribution: for their contributions to normative economic theory, particularly regarding equality of opportunity and fair allocation
nominations.rationale: Their work formally integrates the philosophical concepts of responsibility and equal opportunity into normative economic theory. This provides a vital, rigorous framework for the evaluation of institutional discrimination and social inequality.

nominations.contribution: for his application of structural and empirical methods to welfare economics, tax policy, and labor supply
nominations.rationale: His integration of deep institutional knowledge with structural and quasi-experimental methods provides robust foundations for empirically measuring the true welfare impacts of tax and labor supply policies.

nominations.contribution: for their theoretical and experimental incorporation of fairness, reciprocity, and inequality aversion into economic models
nominations.rationale: Their incorporation of fairness, reciprocity, and inequality aversion into economic theory significantly expanded welfare economics, aligning normative models with the realistic social preferences and constraints of individuals.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to welfare economics and the integration of natural capital into the measurement of social well-being
nominations.rationale: His rigorous theoretical contributions to welfare economics elegantly integrate the valuation of natural capital, providing a vital framework for understanding intergenerational equity and long-run sustainable well-being.

nominations.contribution: for his rigorous theoretical contributions to modeling bounded rationality and decision-making
nominations.rationale: His mathematically rigorous contributions to economic theory provide fundamental tools for modeling welfare and decision-making when agents face bounded rationality or complex institutional environments.

nominations.contribution: for their foundational contributions to behavioral welfare economics
key_works: Bernheim & Rangel, 2004: Addiction and Cue-Triggered Decision Processes, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: By incorporating psychological realism into economic models, they have developed rigorous normative criteria for evaluating consumer welfare when individuals make behavioral mistakes. This is crucial for assessing policies like sin taxes and consumer protection.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to the measurement and theoretical understanding of long-run economic inequality
key_works: Piketty, 2003: Income Inequality in France, 1901-1998, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: Piketty's painstaking construction of historical tax data revolutionized our empirical knowledge of income and wealth distributions. Confronting macro-level growth models with detailed micro-level distributional data has redefined welfare economics.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to general equilibrium theory with incomplete markets and the leverage cycle
key_works: Geanakoplos, 2010: The Leverage Cycle, NBER Macroeconomics Annual
nominations.rationale: Geanakoplos extended general equilibrium to realistic settings where risk cannot be perfectly insured, profoundly changing our understanding of financial markets. His models show exactly how collateral constraints and leverage drive broader welfare outcomes.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to microeconomic theory, fairness, and the economics of information
key_works: Varian, 1974: Equity, Envy, and Efficiency, Journal of Economic Theory
nominations.rationale: Varian's theoretical work on fairness provided a highly tractable way to evaluate welfare without arbitrary social welfare functions. Furthermore, his later work on the economics of information and search has been deeply influential for modern product markets.

nominations.contribution: for their development of the theory of equality of opportunity and responsibility-sensitive egalitarianism
key_works: Roemer, 1998: Equality of Opportunity, Harvard University Press
nominations.rationale: Their work introduces precise mathematical structures to differentiate between inequalities arising from effort versus circumstance. This sophisticated approach to welfare criteria has a direct bearing on optimal taxation and social policy.

nominations.contribution: for his fundamental contributions to the rigorous formulation of general equilibrium theory
key_works: Mas-Colell, 1985: The Theory of General Economic Equilibrium: A Differentiable Approach, Cambridge University Press
nominations.rationale: He established the definitive microeconomic foundations ensuring that preferences and technologies aggregate consistently. His work is the mathematical bedrock for disciplined structural macroeconomics.

nominations.contribution: for his theoretical analysis of social and economic networks and their implications for general equilibrium
key_works: Jackson and Wolinsky, 1996: A Strategic Model of Social and Economic Networks, Journal of Economic Theory
nominations.rationale: He offered tractable tools to model localized micro-interactions that scale up into systemic aggregate outcomes. This greatly advanced the analytical capacity of general-equilibrium network theory.

nominations.contribution: for his general equilibrium models of risk-sharing and financial contracting in developing economies
key_works: Townsend, 1994: Risk and Insurance in Village India, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: He confronted canonical dynamic general-equilibrium risk-sharing theories with meticulously gathered long-run household expenditure data. His integration of deep structural models with microdata is exemplary.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to welfare economics and the measurement of social progress
nominations.rationale: He incorporated complex equity considerations and heterogeneous preferences into formal general equilibrium settings. This expands aggregate welfare measurement without sacrificing axiomatic rigor.

nominations.contribution: for his formalization of equality of opportunity and normative welfare criteria in economic systems
nominations.rationale: He provided a disciplined mathematical translation of philosophically complex distributive concepts into standard economic theory. His formal mechanisms demonstrate robust theoretical bounds on inequality.

nominations.contribution: for their axiomatic analysis of fair allocation and cost sharing
key_works: Moulin, 2003: Fair Division and Collective Welfare, MIT Press
Young, 1994: Equity: In Theory and Practice, Princeton University Press
nominations.rationale: Moulin and Young's axiomatic characterization of equitable allocation rules establishes the fundamental impossibility and possibility frontiers that form the theoretical bedrock for designing fair mechanisms without prices.

nominations.contribution: for their foundational contributions to the theory of fair allocation and the concept of envy-freeness
key_works: Foley, 1967: Resource Allocation and the Public Sector, Yale Economic Essays
Varian, 1974: Equity, Envy, and Efficiency, Journal of Economic Theory
nominations.rationale: Foley and Varian introduced and mathematically formalized the concept of envy-freeness, an essential normative criterion that evaluates mechanism stability and equity in modern resource allocation.

nominations.contribution: for his rigorous axiomatic analysis of fair allocation rules and social choice
key_works: Thomson, 2011: Fair Allocation Rules, Handbook of Social Choice and Welfare
nominations.rationale: Thomson's sweeping work organizes the abstract microeconomic theory of fair division into clear, actionable axioms, illuminating the trade-offs mechanism designers face in indivisible allocations.

nominations.contribution: for their contributions to welfare economics and the formalization of equality of opportunity
key_works: Roemer, 1998: Equality of Opportunity, Harvard University Press
nominations.rationale: By moving beyond simple outcome equality to formalize equality of opportunity, they enrich welfare theory, allowing for mechanism design to account for individual responsibility and structural constraints.

nominations.contribution: for his mathematical and axiomatic methods in economic theory and bounded rationality
key_works: Rubinstein, 1982: Perfect Equilibrium in a Bargaining Model, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: Rubinstein’s profound axiomatic approach rigorously delineates what can and cannot be achieved in bargaining and strategic environments, offering essential mathematical discipline to the field of general equilibrium and games.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of aggregate excess demand and the limits of uniqueness and stability in general equilibrium

Fleurbaey and Maniquet, 2011: A Theory of Fairness and Social Welfare, Cambridge University Press
nominations.rationale: The contribution gives welfare economics a precise language for separating circumstances from choices. This distinction has clear relevance for democratic legitimacy and for the evaluation of public policy across societies.

Magill and Quinzii, 1996: Theory of Incomplete Markets, MIT Press

Thomson, 1983: The Fair Division of a Fixed Supply among a Growing Population, Mathematics of Operations Research
Moulin and Thomson, 1988: Can Everyone Benefit from Growth? Two Difficulties, Journal of Mathematical Economics
nominations.rationale: Their work provided precise criteria for evaluating fair division, rationing and allocation rules. From an institutional perspective, it is valuable because it tells us what different allocation procedures imply normatively before they are implemented in policy.

nominations.contribution: for the theory of equality of opportunity, responsibility and social welfare
key_works: Roemer, 1998: Equality of Opportunity, Harvard University Press
Fleurbaey, 2008: Fairness, Responsibility, and Welfare, Oxford University Press
Fleurbaey and Maniquet, 2011: A Theory of Fairness and Social Welfare, Cambridge University Press
nominations.rationale: This work sharpened the distinction between inequality due to circumstances, effort and institutional responsibility. I would value it because it gives empirical researchers clearer normative targets when measuring intergenerational inequality and policy effects.

nominations.contribution: for welfare analysis of sustainability and intergenerational well-being
key_works: Dasgupta and Heal, 1974: The Optimal Depletion of Exhaustible Resources, Review of Economic Studies
Dasgupta, 2001: Human Well-Being and the Natural Environment, Oxford University Press
Dasgupta, 2021: The Economics of Biodiversity: The Dasgupta Review, HM Treasury
nominations.rationale: Dasgupta extended welfare economics to intergenerational well-being, natural capital and sustainability. While some of the applications reach beyond the narrow field boundary, the core contribution is a welfare framework for evaluating long-run social outcomes.

name: Richard Friberg

nominations.contribution: for demonstrating the generality and limits of aggregate excess demand in general equilibrium
key_works: Sonnenschein, 1972: Market excess demand functions, Econometrica
Sonnenschein, 1973: Do Walras' identity and continuity characterize the class of community excess demand functions?, Journal of Economic Theory
Mantel, 1974: On the characterization of aggregate excess demand, Journal of Economic Theory
nominations.rationale: This result profoundly changed what general equilibrium theory can and cannot predict from individual rationality alone. I would support it because it clarifies the boundary between elegant theory and empirically restrictive mechanisms.

nominations.contribution: for advancing the mathematical foundations of general equilibrium and differentiable economic analysis

people.name: Andreu Mas-Colell
people.affiliation: Universitat Pompeu Fabra and Barcelona School of Economics

key_works: Mas-Colell, 1974: An equilibrium existence theorem without complete or transitive preferences, Journal of Mathematical Economics
Mas-Colell, 1985: The Theory of General Economic Equilibrium: A Differentiable Approach, Cambridge University Press
Mas-Colell, Whinston and Green, 1995: Microeconomic Theory, Oxford University Press
nominations.rationale: Mas-Colell provided tools and synthesis that shaped modern theoretical economics well beyond one theorem. The work is fundamental, though less directly tied to the micro evidence that I would normally emphasize.

nominations.contribution: for the impossibility theorems on strategy-proof social choice
key_works: Gibbard, 1973: Manipulation of voting schemes: A general result, Econometrica
Satterthwaite, 1975: Strategy-proofness and Arrow's conditions: Existence and correspondence theorems for voting procedures and social welfare functions, Journal of Economic Theory
Gibbard, 1977: Manipulation of schemes that mix voting with chance, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: The contribution identifies a fundamental constraint on collective decision-making under private preferences. Its importance is conceptual and practical for institutional design, even if it lies at the theoretical edge of this field.

nominations.contribution: for axiomatic measurement of poverty, deprivation and multidimensional welfare
key_works: Foster, Greer and Thorbecke, 1984: A class of decomposable poverty measures, Econometrica
Alkire and Foster, 2011: Counting and multidimensional poverty measurement, Journal of Public Economics
Foster, 1984: On economic poverty: A survey of aggregate measures, Advances in Econometrics
nominations.rationale: This contribution gave welfare economics operational measures that governments and researchers can use with household data. I value the combination of axiomatic clarity, decomposability and direct empirical implementation.

nominations.contribution: for axiomatic theories of fair allocation, cost sharing and welfare comparison
key_works: Moulin, 1988: Axioms of Cooperative Decision Making, Cambridge University Press
Thomson, 1994: Cooperative models of bargaining, Handbook of Game Theory
Moulin and Thomson, 1988: Can everyone benefit from growth?, Journal of Mathematical Economics
nominations.rationale: Their work clarified how fairness principles translate into allocation and cost-sharing rules. It is theoretically precise and normatively important, though its empirical footprint is narrower than the leading nominations.

nominations.contribution: for the mathematical foundations of general equilibrium theory

people.name: Andreu Mas-Colell
people.affiliation: Universitat Pompeu Fabra and Barcelona School of Economics

key_works: Mas-Colell, 1974: An Equilibrium Existence Theorem without Complete or Transitive Preferences, Journal of Mathematical Economics
Mas-Colell, 1985: The Theory of General Economic Equilibrium: A Differentiable Approach, Cambridge University Press
Mas-Colell, Whinston and Green, 1995: Microeconomic Theory, Oxford University Press
nominations.rationale: Mas-Colell deepened the analytical foundations on which much of modern equilibrium economics rests. The contribution is foundational, technically elegant and central to the disciplined general-equilibrium thinking that I value.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of general equilibrium with incomplete asset markets
key_works: Geanakoplos and Polemarchakis, 1986: Existence, Regularity, and Constrained Suboptimality of Competitive Allocations When the Asset Market Is Incomplete, in Essays in Honor of Kenneth J. Arrow
Geanakoplos, 1990: An Introduction to General Equilibrium with Incomplete Asset Markets, Journal of Mathematical Economics
Geanakoplos, 2003: Liquidity, Default, and Crashes: Endogenous Contracts in General Equilibrium, in Advances in Economics and Econometrics
nominations.rationale: This work showed how missing markets alter welfare, determinacy and policy in otherwise competitive economies. It is a natural bridge from abstract equilibrium theory to modern macro-financial models with heterogeneity and constraints.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of fair allocation, envy-freeness and resource allocation rules
key_works: Varian, 1974: Equity, Envy, and Efficiency, Journal of Economic Theory
Moulin, 1988: Axioms of Cooperative Decision Making, Cambridge University Press
Thomson, 2011: Fair Allocation Rules, Handbook of Social Choice and Welfare
nominations.rationale: The contribution made distributional fairness operational within rigorous allocation theory. It is attractive because it preserves the discipline of welfare economics while admitting normative criteria beyond efficiency alone.

nominations.contribution: for the measurement and decomposition of inequality and poverty

people.name: Anthony F. Shorrocks
people.affiliation: University of Manchester emeritus and UNU-WIDER

key_works: Bourguignon, 1979: Decomposable Income Inequality Measures, Econometrica
Shorrocks, 1980: The Class of Additively Decomposable Inequality Measures, Econometrica
Cowell, 1980: On the Structure of Additive Inequality Measures, Review of Economic Studies
nominations.rationale: This work supplied the measurement theory that allows distributional facts to be compared across groups, time and economies. For macroeconomics, such measurement discipline is essential before building models of inequality dynamics.

nominations.contribution: for the theory of equality of opportunity and responsibility-sensitive social welfare
key_works: Roemer, 1998: Equality of Opportunity, Harvard University Press
Fleurbaey, 2008: Fairness, Responsibility, and Welfare, Oxford University Press
Fleurbaey and Maniquet, 2011: A Theory of Fairness and Social Welfare, Cambridge University Press
nominations.rationale: This contribution provides rigorous welfare criteria for separating circumstances from responsibility in evaluating allocations. It has influenced how economists formalize normative questions about inequality, redistribution and opportunity.

nominations.contribution: for the axiomatic theory of fair allocation and division

people.name: Hal R. Varian
people.affiliation: University of California, Berkeley, emeritus; Google

key_works: Varian, 1974: Equity, Envy, and Efficiency, Journal of Economic Theory
Moulin, 1988: Axioms of Cooperative Decision Making, Cambridge University Press
Thomson, 2011: Fair Allocation Rules, in Handbook of Social Choice and Welfare
nominations.rationale: This is closest to my own standards: rigorous axioms, sharp trade-offs, and direct relevance to allocating indivisible or scarce resources without ordinary prices. The contribution supplies general principles that travel across public-sector allocation problems.

nominations.contribution: for poverty and inequality measures that connect normative criteria with empirical implementation
key_works: Foster, Greer and Thorbecke, 1984: A Class of Decomposable Poverty Measures, Econometrica
Shorrocks, 1980: The Class of Additively Decomposable Inequality Measures, Econometrica
Bourguignon, 1979: Decomposable Income Inequality Measures, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: The work gave welfare economics usable measurement tools with transparent axiomatic content. I value especially decomposability, because it makes distributional objectives implementable in real policy systems.

nominations.contribution: for the theory of general equilibrium with incomplete markets
key_works: Geanakoplos and Polemarchakis, 1986: Existence, Regularity, and Constrained Suboptimality of Competitive Allocations When the Asset Market Is Incomplete, in Essays in Honor of Kenneth J. Arrow
Magill and Quinzii, 1996: Theory of Incomplete Markets, MIT Press
Geanakoplos, 2010: The Leverage Cycle, NBER Macroeconomics Annual
nominations.rationale: This contribution shows precisely how welfare theorems fail when markets are missing. It is a clean impossibility-and-possibility frontier with major implications for finance and macroeconomic policy.

nominations.contribution: for global and differentiable methods in general equilibrium analysis

people.name: Andreu Mas-Colell
people.affiliation: Universitat Pompeu Fabra and Barcelona School of Economics, emeritus

key_works: Mas-Colell, 1974: An Equilibrium Existence Theorem without Complete or Transitive Preferences, Journal of Mathematical Economics
Balasko, 1975: Some Results on Uniqueness and on Stability of Equilibrium in General Equilibrium Theory, Journal of Mathematical Economics
Mas-Colell, 1985: The Theory of General Economic Equilibrium: A Differentiable Approach, Cambridge University Press
nominations.rationale: This work deepened the mathematical understanding of equilibrium beyond existence. I would see it as worthy because it clarifies the structure and limits of the equilibrium correspondence, not merely because it is technically elegant.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of aggregate excess demand and the limits of general-equilibrium determinacy
key_works: Sonnenschein, 1972: Market Excess Demand Functions, Econometrica
Sonnenschein, 1973: Do Walras' Identity and Continuity Characterize the Class of Community Excess Demand Functions?, Journal of Economic Theory
Shafer and Sonnenschein, 1982: Market Demand and Excess Demand Functions, in Handbook of Mathematical Economics
nominations.rationale: The contribution is a fundamental negative result: individual rationality alone imposes weak restrictions on aggregate demand. Such impossibility results are scientifically valuable because they tell us which institutional or behavioral assumptions are doing real work.
